name: Moses
overview: Moses was a male member of the tribe of Levi who uniquely led Israel out of Egyptian bondage during the Exodus. As a central figure in biblical history, he served as God's chosen deliverer and mediator for the nation of Israel. There are no additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Moses' means 'draw out,' reflecting his role in drawing Israel out of Egypt, as noted in Exodus 2:10. God explicitly gave him the title 'My servant Moses' (Numbers 12:7), emphasizing his role as a faithful servant of the Lord. Other titles such as 'man of God' and 'servant of the LORD' further highlight his devoted service and leadership.
familyAndRelationships: Moses was married to Zipporah and had at least two sons, Gershom and Eliezer. He was the brother of Aaron and Miriam, and his father was Amram and his mother Jochebed. His brother-in-law was Hobab. Importantly, he is identified as the servant of YHVH, underscoring his unique relationship with God.
scriptureSignificance: Moses holds a pivotal role as the great lawgiver and prophet who led God's people out of slavery in Egypt, establishing the covenant relationship through the giving of the Law. His leadership spanned forty years in the wilderness, during which he mediated God's commands and guidance to Israel. Although he was not permitted to enter the Promised Land, his life prefigures Christ as the ultimate deliverer and mediator between God and humanity.
